title: Telemetry incident response policy (legacy)
text: Legacy telemetry incidents had a sixteen-business-hour initial response target. This version was superseded and must not be used for current servicing decisions.

title: Telemetry incident response policy — Standard tier
text: For an active Standard subscription to PRD-TELEMETRY, the initial response target for a service-impacting telemetry incident is eight business hours. Escalation review occurs after two consecutive failed synchronization windows.

title: Telemetry incident response policy — Premium tier
text: For an active Premium subscription to PRD-TELEMETRY, the initial response target for a service-impacting telemetry incident is two clock hours. Escalation review occurs after three consecutive degraded synchronization windows or any confirmed data-loss event.

title: Telemetry incident response policy — proposed revision
text: Draft proposal for a one-hour telemetry response target. This document is unapproved and is not authoritative.

title: Diagnosing delayed telemetry batches
text: Delayed telemetry batches can follow repeated connector retries. Support should compare synchronization-window timestamps, confirm whether batches eventually arrive, and distinguish latency from data loss before recommending reindexing.

title: Tier 2 investigation note for CASE-4821
text: CASE-4821 remains under investigation. It was escalated after three consecutive synchronization windows exceeded the latency baseline. Tier 2 observed connector retries, while the delayed batches reviewed so far eventually arrived. This is not a definitive root cause and does not prove that no data-loss event occurred outside the reviewed windows. A controlled index integrity check and possible rebuild are scheduled for the November 8 maintenance window; the record does not confirm that either action was completed. Support requested connector diagnostic logs for the affected windows, but receipt of those logs is not recorded. No confirmed root cause or resolution date is available.

title: Outstanding diagnostics request for CASE-4821
text: Support requested connector diagnostic logs covering the three delayed synchronization windows. Receipt of the requested logs is not recorded, so the evidence cannot establish whether the logs were sent or what they might show. The missing record is not evidence that the customer declined the request.

title: November 8 telemetry maintenance plan
text: A telemetry maintenance window is scheduled for November 8 from 02:00 to 03:00 UTC. The plan permits an index integrity check and a rebuild only if validation indicates one is needed. A schedule is not proof that either action ran or completed; completion requires a separate maintenance result record.

title: Customer call transcript for CASE-4821
text: Maya reported that telemetry appeared forty to sixty minutes late during three evening synchronization windows. She confirmed that the delayed readings eventually appeared and asked for an explanation before the next reporting cycle.

title: Investigation note for CASE-4824
text: CASE-4824 tracks intermittent telemetry export latency for Northstar Bikes. One synchronization window failed and the following retry completed normally; the Standard-tier escalation threshold has not been reached.

title: Updating a billing contact
text: A billing-contact update requires a verified account administrator. Support may explain the verification steps but cannot change the billing contact from this servicing assistant.

title: Billing contact verification policy
text: For active PRD-BILLING subscriptions, a billing-contact change requires verification of an account administrator. The servicing assistant may provide guidance but is not authorized to perform the change.

title: Resolution note for CASE-4822
text: Customer Operations verified an authorized Northstar Bikes account administrator at 13:55 UTC. The billing-contact update was completed in the billing system at 14:08 UTC, and Luis confirmed the corrected contact at 14:12 UTC. CASE-4822 was marked Resolved at 14:15 UTC.

title: Mobile dashboard incident response policy — Standard tier
text: For an active Standard subscription to PRD-DASHBOARD, the initial response target for a service-impacting mobile dashboard incident is twelve business hours. Investigation may pause while support awaits the application version and a reproducible event timestamp from the customer.

title: Customer follow-up note for CASE-4823
text: The CASE-4823 dashboard refresh issue was not reproduced during the documented support attempt. That result does not prove the issue did not occur. Support requested the mobile application version and a timestamp from Priya before continuing the investigation; receipt of those details is not recorded.

title: Resolution note for CASE-4825
text: For CASE-4825, Tier 2 confirmed an expired connector certificate blocked telemetry exports. The certificate rotation was completed at 11:35 UTC, the queued export replay completed at 12:10 UTC, and monitoring confirmed the backlog cleared at 12:30 UTC. The case was marked Resolved at 12:40 UTC. These completed actions apply only to CASE-4825 and must not be inferred for CASE-4821.
